# Abstract {.unnumbered}

Aircraft cabin lighting is built from many RGBW LED segments along the cabin, and all segments have to change their light at the same time. In the system of AES Aircraft Elektro/Elektronik System GmbH, the segments are connected in a daisy chain, and a master sends the brightness values to all segments with the serial protocol Flexlink. This thesis designs the digital control and forwarding part of such a segment, implements it on a Cologne Chip GateMate FPGA with a completely open-source tool flow (Yosys, nextpnr and openFPGALoader) and tests it on real hardware.

The requirements were taken from the AES documents. They ask for four channels with 16-bit dimming, a PWM frequency above 400 Hz, identical nodes in a daisy chain and an update of 25 segments within 25 ms. A timing analysis shows that the 25 ms limit can only be met if each node forwards the data word by word (cut-through) instead of first storing the whole packet. A Simulink model of the data path was built as a first reference. The node itself was written as one synthesizable Verilog design that runs as the same bitstream on every node. It keeps its own brightness values, forwards the rest of the packet, numbers the nodes with a Count Segments packet, sends the answers of all nodes back in the order of the chain and generates four 16-bit PWM signals.

A prototype with two GateMate boards, a PC as master and red, green, blue and white LEDs confirmed the design. The PWM frequency is 763 Hz with a step of one clock cycle of 20 ns, and the forwarding delay is 10.69 µs per node. With this delay, 25 segments are updated in about 2.5 ms, one tenth of the limit. All 14 robustness tests with wrong or broken packets gave the expected result. The design uses 1.9 % of the logic of the FPGA and reaches 68.8 MHz, so it is small and leaves room for later extensions. Open points are mainly in the analog part, the electrical limits of the evaluation board and features such as a temperature sensor.
